chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, who said:

Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda' died while I was in Medina, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sent me a dinar and said: 'Buy embalming material with this, and know that the embalming material is camphor, but do as the people do.' He said: 'So when I went, he followed me with a dinar and said: 'Buy camphor with this.'

key_terms.أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ الْحَذَّاءُ: Abu Ubaydah the Shoemaker, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.حَنُوط: Embalming material or powder used for the deceased
key_terms.دِينَار: A gold coin used as currency

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using camphor for embalming the deceased according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia scholarly principle of balancing textual precision with social adaptability (urf), as Imam al-Sadiq (AS) initially instructed following the general public's usage of the term 'hanut' before clarifying the specific preference for camphor. It highlights the practical jurisprudence of funeral rites, emphasizing that while specific substances like camphor are preferred for their aromatic and preservative qualities, the ritual validity is not strictly bound to technical definitions if the community's custom is followed. This dual approach reflects the Imams' wisdom in maintaining religious authenticity while accommodating local cultural practices.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Dawood Bin Sirham who said,

‘Abu Ubeyda Al-Haza’a died and I was in Al-Medina, so Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> sent a Dinar to me and said: ‘Buy embalming (material), and know that the embalming (material), it is the camphor, but do as what the people are doing’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘So when I went, he<sup>asws</sup> followed me with a Dinar and said: ‘Buy camphor with this’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Dawud ibn Sarhan who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Ubaydah al-Hadhdha’ died and I was in al-Madinah. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, sent a dinar and said, ‘Buy with it hunut and take notice that hunut is camphor; however, do as people do.’ When I went, he (the Imam) sent a dinar and said, ‘Buy camphor with it.’”
